cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a woman's beaded head ornament with metal plaques, coins, and glass beadwork strung on cloth strips — a type of adornment consistent with Khanty (and neighboring Siberian/Uralic peoples') traditional dress, plausible for the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: head-ornament
physical.summary: A woman's head ornament; made of beads, metal and cloth.  Dark brown wool woven cloth stitched to front of two strips of cloth (made of natural cream tabby linen) sewn together at top.  Square-shaped silver-coloured metal plaques (each made up of four separate 'roundels') stitched in a vertical line to each strip.  Edged with couched threaded black and white glass (?) beads.  Larger threaded blue and white glass (?) beads stitched in a few places on top; most left free and decorated at ends with white and green beadwork and brass discs and crosses, and metal coins with two small holes pierced in the centre.  Attached to right side (as worn) of head ornament is a blue and white cotton ribbon, commercially woven, wrapped around tabby wool strip.  Opposite side has much of tie missing, including cotton ribbon.
